artworks.title: Study for "War and Peace"
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with wash on wove paper mounted to paperboard
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1950)
artworks.description: The image shows a person in a full-body sketch, upright and slightly turned to the left. The person is facing sideways with their head slightly up. Their hair is styled in an updo, and they wear a long robe with voluminous sleeves and a possible cloak. The person is holding a branch in their left hand. Next to them is a large block or pedestal. The background is plain with light shading framing the figure.

artworks.title: Group of Figures
artworks.medium: charcoal on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1950)
artworks.description: The image shows a group of figures in a sketchy and textured style. Their bodies are primarily depicted in full, with most appearing seated or kneeling and facing a central figure. The central person is larger and standing upright, slightly bent forward. All individuals have obscured facial features and indistinguishable hair. Clothing is roughly drawn with shadowy strokes, suggesting heavy garments. Surrounding the figures are more lightly sketched forms, hinting at a cluster of people. The setting is lacking specific details, with a dark and hazy background, creating a mysterious atmosphere.

artworks.title: Vue ... et elévation des ... omnibus du boulevard ...
artworks.medium: lithograph
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Dr. Armand Hammer)
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an omnibus. The drawing depicts a horse-drawn omnibus with exaggerated features. It appears to be overfilled with passengers, some wearing top hats. The body of the omnibus is detailed, and the passengers are drawn with exaggerated expressions and proportions. Figures on the roof seem precariously balanced, with one figure attempting to climb aboard from the side. The style is typical of 19th-century satirical cartooning.

artworks.title: Marsh in Zeeland
artworks.medium: watercolor and gouache on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Bequest of James Parmelee, 1941)
artworks.description: The image shows a low-angle view of a landscape with fields stretching into the distance. The horizon is in the upper third of the composition, blending with the sky. Some architectural structures can be seen along the horizon, including a dome and other silhouettes hinting at a town or cityscape. The brushstrokes are soft and washed, with a watercolor technique providing a loose texture. The color palette includes muted greens and browns for the foreground, while the background has soft grays and blues. In the foreground field, a figure stands, adding scale to the scene.

artworks.title: Lake Houses
artworks.medium: charcoal on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Museum Purchase, Membership Association Fund, 1953)
artworks.description: The image depicts a waterside scene from a direct point of view. The horizon shows softly outlined hills or mountains. In the middle ground, there are lines representing a water body, a building, boats, and trees. The color palette is mainly shades of gray due to the pencil sketch technique, creating a serene atmosphere.

artworks.title: Self-Portrait [recto]
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Margerite A. C. Stewart, 1963)
artworks.description: The image is a pencil sketch of an adult male subject's head and part of his neck. The subject's head faces slightly left with a neutral expression. He has a broad forehead, dense beard, closely cut hairstyle, and the shading emphasizes the contours of his face. The subject wears a collared garment. There is no visible jewelry or objects. The background is plain with minimal detail, except for a faint sketch on the upper left. Handwritten text below the image identifies it as a self-portrait by "Wm. E. Winner" from around 1880 in Philadelphia and includes a note about ownership.

artworks.title: A Street in Tangiers
artworks.medium: watercolor on paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: Seven men sit or stand in a town street in front of a bone-brown stucco building in this horizontal watercolor painting. Light pours across the road from the right, making the surface glow parchment white. The building is close to us and takes up the left two-thirds of the composition. Its face is flat except for a wide, deeply shadowed arch, which is about twice the height of the standing person, and a shallowly projecting structure that encases the second story of the corner. This structure is pierced to create intricate tracery and is supported by corbels. Three people sit or recline against the building façade in the middle of the composition. They wear tattered clothing in ivory white, scarlet red, ultramarine blue, beige, and black. Their skin is painted in tones of ash white, and they have beards. Their eyes appear to be closed. One man hunches over a long staff across his lap, and the head of another man rests back against the wall, his mouth downturned and eyebrows gathered. The reclining person’s bare legs stretch long, and his slippers lie near bare feet as he props his head in one hand. A fourth man is wrapped in white cloth and stands looking at the trio, facing away from us. A fifth man perches atop a donkey, swaddled in pale peach and white fabric and huddled around a long rifle braced upright in front of him. Now we realize that the long staff the other man held is also the barrel of a rifle. A second pale donkey stands in profile facing our left in front of the mounted man, who looks down at a man who returns his gaze as he stands behind that second donkey. In the right third of the watercolor is a view down an alley-like street spanned occasionally with arches or walkways. People man tables set out in front of the buildings there and others look at the wares. Another man swathed in black fabric huddles near the corner of the building. The artist inscribed and dated the lower right corner of the watercolor, “A M Stewart son ami Fortuny 1869.”

artworks.title: Launching the Life Boat
artworks.medium: black lithographic crayon on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Childs Bruen Perkins, 1945)
artworks.description: The image depicts a group of figures interacting with a boat on water. The drawing is created with loose and expressive lines emphasizing movement. In the center, figures seem to be propelling or guiding the boat. The background includes flowing lines and a few defined creases, representing a shoreline and distant landmasses. The style appears impressionistic, focusing on action and environment over details.

artworks.title: Two Dogs
artworks.medium: black lithographic crayon on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Childs Bruen Perkins, 1945)

artworks.title: Near Hope Gate, Quebec
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mrs. Childs Bruen Perkins, 1945)
artworks.description: The image shows a raised view of a sloping street. A paved walkway runs alongside a stone wall towards houses in the distance. Buildings are seen on the left side of the slope. In the background, there is a horizon with buildings in the distance. The painting features fine, detailed brushstrokes and a subtle color palette dominated by pale tones, gray, and sepia hues.

artworks.title: Dordrecht
artworks.medium: graphite on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image shows a street view from a slightly elevated point, allowing the viewer to look into an archway that frames a couple in the distance. The focus is on the architectural detailing of the archway and the space beyond it. The arch appears to be ornate, showcasing intricate designs and carvings typical of an older architectural style. The drawing is in monochrome, created with pencil or charcoal, depicting a soft contrast between light and shadow. The strokes vary, with denser shading around the archway for depth and lighter strokes where the couple stands, suggesting light hitting the surface. The palette consists of shades of grey, giving the sketch a classic and subdued atmosphere, emphasizing the play of light and shadow in the scene.

artworks.title: Two Male Nudes
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink on laid paper
artworks.dimensions:
other (French mat): 15 7/8 x 11 1/2 in. (40.32 x 29.21 cm)
sight: 13 x 8 5/8 in. (33.02 x 21.91 cm)
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (William A. Clark Collection, 1926)
artworks.description: Two male figures are depicted in a sketched illustration. Both figures are shown from head to toe in an upright position, showcasing muscular anatomy. The figure on the left faces left with a slightly turned head, while the figure on the right faces forward with the head slightly downward. The faces are minimally detailed, with a focus on body structure rather than facial features. The hair is illustrated with loose, stylized curls. The figures are nude, emphasizing their defined muscles. The background features a textured sketch paper appearance, creating an aged look.

artworks.title: Preliminary Drawing for "A Donkey-Team (Attelage d'ânes)"
artworks.medium: graphite and black conté crayon on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Carl Feiss, 1971)
artworks.description: The image depicts a young boy holding the reins of two adorned horses. The horses are shown with detailed features in a line-drawn style. In the background, there are buildings, a bridge over water, and a staircase leading up to a street level with a horse-drawn cart and a driver. The art style features fine pencil-like lines, textured patterns, and a monochromatic color palette of brown and beige, lending a vintage effect.

artworks.title: Three Figures
artworks.medium: ink heightened with white
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: Three individuals are depicted standing upright in elaborate robes and hats. The figure on the left is in profile, facing right, with a mustache. The middle figure has their back to the viewer, wearing a large hat and cloak. The figure on the right is in profile facing the left individual, wearing a large hat and robes with a collar. The middle figure carries a long object, and the right figure holds a sword or stick. The background is plain.

artworks.title: Youth Holding a Dish
artworks.medium: red and black chalk with touches of white (partially oxydized) on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image portrays the upper two-thirds of a person's body holding a spherical object in one hand. The person's head is tilted to one side with a gentle expression on their face, featuring soft and subtle shading around the eyes, nose, and mouth. The person has wavy hair framing their face, depicted with flowing lines. They are shown wearing minimal clothing with a textured fabric draping across their torso. The background is a plain, neutral tone.

artworks.title: Young Man
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with brown wash
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image features the upper body of a person standing with one hand on their waist. Their facial features show a serene expression with a slight turn and smooth complexion. They wear a garment with vertical pleats or stripes, covering their arms, and a hat partially covering their hair. The background is plain, and "Paolo Uccello" is written in the lower-left corner of the image.

artworks.title: Promenade near a French Country Estate
artworks.medium: watercolor and gouache on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Lady Inchyra, 1962)
artworks.description: The image depicts a tranquil outdoor setting with a group of people in period attire walking on a grassy field. In the background, there are distant trees, hills, a pale sky, a man with a horse and cart, a house, a stone wall with a gate, and tall trees framing a structure. The scene is painted with gentle brushstrokes and a color palette of earth tones, soft greens, and muted reds.

artworks.title: Vicinity of Morestal
artworks.medium: watercolor and fabricated charcoal
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image depicts a landscape at sunset. The view is from a low vantage, showing a flat expanse stretching towards the horizon. The horizon line divides the sky from the land and reflects water below. Silhouettes on the horizon could be trees or man-made structures, highlighted by the setting sun's glow. Loose, impressionistic brushstrokes capture the light and atmosphere. The color palette is warm, with earth tones of brown, ochre, and amber blending together, contrasted by hints of blue and violet. Earthy tones in the foreground suggest marsh or wetland, while the background shows a gradient of colors blending into the sky.

artworks.title: Environs de Cremieu
artworks.medium: watercolor and graphite on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: The image depicts a landscape with a slightly elevated perspective. The horizon line is positioned above the center, showing distant hills under a warmly glowing sky. In the foreground, bare trees with thin, twisting branches are depicted. The painting uses soft and blended brushstrokes, creating a sense of gentle motion. The color palette includes warm earth tones, rich browns, deep reds, light blues, and yellows, along with pastel hues in the sky.

artworks.title: The Pigeons
artworks.medium: pen and sepia ink over graphite on off-white wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of E. Gerald Lamboley, 1993)
artworks.description: The image depicts three women and a child engaged in conversation near a tree. Two women are seated holding a child, and another woman is crouched nearby. The background shows distant landscape elements such as trees and bushes. The artwork is detailed, featuring soft pencil strokes in a monochrome palette of graphite grays. Elegantly drawn trees frame the scene.

artworks.title: Natural Bridge, Virginia
artworks.medium: watercolor and gouache over graphite on paperboard
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: Against a watery blue sky, an arched rock formation joins tall cliffs that together fill most of this vertical watercolor painting. The arch is to our left, next to a plant-covered, tall outcropping. The cliffs dominate the right half of the composition. Lit from the upper left, the rocky faces are light and caramel brown with fog-gray fissures and cracks. The tops of the cliffs are fringed with dark green shrubs and a few long vines hang down some of them. A slate-blue river, dotted with rocks, winds from the lower center of the picture around to our left, before disappearing behind tall boulders there. Near the lower right corner and tiny in scale, a man wearing light blue and tan garments stands on the river’s edge holding fishing pole over the water. Upon closer inspection, a series of small dots of color suggest people crossing the top of the arched bridge. Above them, a buff-white and pale blue sky fills the top third of the scene.

artworks.title: David and Bathsheba
artworks.medium: ink and brown ink with gray wash
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a large gathering in a historical setting. The scene shows many people gathered in a ceremonial or regal setting. The individuals wear elaborate period costumes, including robes and crowns, indicating a scene of royalty or nobility. The background features architecture resembling a grand palace, with ornate columns and archways. Figures are gathered around a bridge that spans the landscape. There is lush greenery and distant structures in the background. The drawing is detailed, showing textures and fabrics, capturing a historical event or narrative.

artworks.title: Landscape with a Cow
artworks.medium: watercolor on wove paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Edward C. and Mary Walker Collection, 1937)
artworks.description: The image depicts a rural scene from a slightly elevated perspective. The horizon line is low in the composition, with an expansive sky dominating the upper portion. On the horizon, there is a line of trees or bushes. In the foreground, a brown and white cow grazes near a wooden fence that directs the viewer's eye diagonally. More cows are visible in the distance, along with a cluster of trees to the right. Loose and light brushstrokes are used, typical of a watercolor technique, giving an airy quality to the scene. The color palette is soft and muted, with earthy greens and browns in the land, and pale blue and beige hues in the sky, creating a serene atmosphere.

artworks.title: Study of Orpheus for "Classic and Romantic Art"
artworks.medium: charcoal on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Corcoran Collection (Gift of Miss Emily Sargent and Mrs. Francis Ormond, sisters of the artist, 1949)
artworks.description: The image is a sketch of a man standing upright with his body slightly turned to the side. His arms are flexed away from his chest, and his head is slightly tilted upwards. The man has strong cheekbones, a prominent jawline, and short, neatly groomed hair. He appears unclothed, showcasing his muscular form. The background is plain, with no distractions around him.
